claims.claim: Mylan acquired EpiPen marketing rights in 2007 when annual sales were near two hundred million dollars.
claims.episode_span: Mylan acquired marketing rights in 2007 when annual sales sat near two hundred million dollars;
claims.supporting_quote: When Mylan acquired the EpiPen, the drug was making about $200 million a year.

claims.claim: The FDA approved neffy epinephrine nasal spray on August 9, 2024 for patients weighing at least 30 kg.
claims.episode_span: ARS Pharmaceuticals developed neffy, the first FDA-approved epinephrine nasal spray, after four clinical studies in 175 adults demonstrated blood levels comparable to injected products. The August 2024 approval covers patients weighing at least thirty kilograms
claims.source_title: FDA Approves First Nasal Spray for Treatment of Anaphylaxis
claims.supporting_quote: Today, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved neffy (epinephrine nasal spray) for the emergency treatment of allergic reactions (Type I), including those that are life-threatening (anaphylaxis), in adult and pediatric patients who weigh at least 30 kilograms (about 66 pounds).

claims.claim: Sheldon Kaplan adapted the military auto-injector design at Survival Technology, leading to EpiPen FDA approval in December 1987.
claims.episode_span: Engineer Sheldon Kaplan, working at Survival Technology, adapted the spring-loaded glass-cartridge design for civilian use in the 1970s, leading to FDA approval of the EpiPen in December 1987.
claims.source_title: Who Owns EpiPen: Viatris, Pfizer, and Pricing
claims.supporting_quote: In the 1970s, engineer Sheldon Kaplan, working at Survival Technology, Inc., recognized that the same mechanism could deliver epinephrine to civilians experiencing life-threatening allergic reactions. His redesigned device became the EpiPen, which the FDA first approved on December 22, 1987.
